text:
maria.k: Quick sync — during the multi-region cutover test we observed ~2% of requests from tenant-47 land in non-resident region while prewarm still in progress. No data leak, just higher latency + audit log entries. Thinking we need a clear cutover policy.
jonathan: Can you paste the minimal repro / logs?
maria.k: gist: request -> routed to region-b, region-b returns 403-residency-check then proxy retries to region-a. Seen retries spike.
akshay: 2% is low but spikes matter. Options: 1) strict reject until cutover complete, 2) allow soft-failover with telemetry tag, 3) proxy-level sticky-queue until resident cache primed.
devon: SLA question: if we strict reject we break availability during cutovers. Is that acceptable for enterprise tenants?
carla: we should expose tenant-level policy: residency=required | best-effort | best-effort-redacted. Teams can pick.
maria.k: Agree on per-tenant policy. But need to define how enforcement happens: control plane validation vs data-plane proxy enforcement. Both have tradeoffs.
jonathan: Control plane: simpler auditing, can prevent auth tokens from being issued outside region. But slower to react to infra drift. Data-plane: fast, localized, but more surface area to update.
akshay: Also consider a "shadow-lease" approach: when primary prewarms, write a shadow marker to regional kv that proxies can read with eventual consistency. Marker TTL ~= prewarm window.
devon: Shadow-lease sounds neat but increases write amplification and relies on kv convergence. What about leaky bucket of retries on proxy to avoid cascading failures?
maria.k: Prototype idea: proxy attempts resident route first. If miss, check shadow-lease key (get with small staleness window). If present -> route; if absent -> consult control-plane cache for tenant policy (fetched async) and act accordingly.
carla: That hybrid keeps enforcement fast with central override. Also gives us per-tenant config for strict/permissive.
jonathan: What about telemetry? We need a clear flag in logs: residency_status=[resident|shadow|cross-region] so billing and audits can query.
akshay: +1. Also push a metric for cross-region count and latency delta per-tenant. We can trigger canary alert if cross-region > X% for Y mins.
sre-bot: deploy:prewarm-check started for region-b (build 2026.3.12)
maria.k: Implementation notes: small proxy change to consult shadow-lease key with 50ms timeout, control-plane endpoint for tenant policy (cached 10s), metric tags as jon suggested. Need migration plan for existing tenants -> default to best-effort.
devon: Migration: notify enterprise tenants with residency=required 30d before change. Default best-effort for others.
carla: Security: if tenant picks best-effort-redacted, we must ensure PII redaction happens pre-route. That implies token-level metadata for redaction hints. Ops complexity spike.
akshay: Tradeoffs summary in two lines: strict enforcement = safer for compliance, breaks availability; hybrid (shadow+control) = best balance but adds complexity and kv load.
maria.k: Proposal: open short RFC (1-pager) with design sketch + perf test plan. Implement hybrid as opt-in feature behind feature flag. Roll to GA after 2-weeks canary.
jonathan: Sounds good. Action items: @akshay prototype shadow-lease write + read test, @devon draft migration notice for enterprise tenants, @carla write security checklist for redaction flow, @maria.k open RFC and assign.
maria.k: I'll open RFC today and link this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
